content: Dirithromycin is no longer available in the United States. If you are currently taking this medication, you should contact your doctor immediately to discuss transitioning to an alternative treatment. Dirithromycin is an antibiotic that is prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including bronchitis, pneumonia, and infections of the skin and throat. It is important to note that antibiotics like dirithromycin are ineffective against viral infections such as the common cold or influenza. In some cases, dirithromycin may be prescribed for conditions not listed here; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. Dirithromycin is supplied as an enteric-coated tablet intended for oral administration. It is typically taken once daily for a duration of 7 to 14 days. You must follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions or concerns, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Swallow the tablets whole; do not chew, crush, or cut them. Always take the medication with a full glass of water. Even if you start feeling better, continue taking dirithromycin for the full prescribed course unless directed otherwise by your doctor. Before starting dirithromycin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any known allergies to dirithromycin, azithromycin, clarithromycin, erythromycin, or any other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially if they include other antibiotics, anticoagulants like warfarin, astemizole, carbamazepine, cisapride, clozapine, cyclosporine, digoxin, disopyramide, ergotamine, felodipine, lovastatin, phenytoin, pimozide, antacids, cimetidine, ranitidine, theophylline, triazolam, or any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, jaundice, colitis, or gastrointestinal issues. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Should you become pregnant while taking dirithromycin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking dirithromycin. Dirithromycin should be taken with food or within one hour of eating. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is nearly time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Dirithromycin may cause side effects. Minor side effects include upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach cramps, mild skin rash, stomach pain, and headache. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. These include severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, unusual fatigue, or signs of a vaginal infection. If you experience any of these serious side effects, contact your doctor immediately. You or your doctor may also report adverse effects to the FDA's MedWatch program. Store dirithromycin in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep the medication at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be required to monitor your response to the medication. Do not share this medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the prescribed course, contact your doctor. The brand name for dirithromycin is Dynabac®.
